mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the negative rank IC is less than 0.08.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC drops below 0.07.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 5-year averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered dual-shock episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.06.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 10-year moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 10-year MA by > 10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the positive rank IC is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending pullback and reduced corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is below 0.04.
